name: Self-Generated In-Context Examples Improve LLM Agents for Sequential Decision-Making Tasks
authors: Vishnu Sarukkai, Zhiqiang Xie, Kayvon Fatahalian (Stanford University)
venue: NeurIPS 2025 (poster); prior version at ICML 2025 Workshop (PUT)
reflection_type: none (no verbal self-critique); self-improvement is via accumulating/curating self-generated successful trajectories as retrieved in-context examples, analogous to reward-weighted regression. Reflection in the verbal-critique sense is explicitly NOT used: failed trajectories are discarded to avoid step-level attribution ambiguity.
feedback_source: environment-reward (binary task success/failure signal); a trajectory is retained only if the episode succeeds. No external tool verifier beyond the environment's own success check, no human, no ground-truth label per step.
iteration_structure: episodic-retry-with-reset across many tasks: agent runs ReAct episodes, appends successful trajectories to a database, and that database serves as in-context examples for future tasks. Database curation uses a population/evolutionary mechanism (population-based training: M parallel agent-database pairs, periodically copying the best DB into the worst).
reflection_object: action trajectory (full reasoning+action traces) stored and reused as in-context examples; equivalently the prompt/context is modified at inference via the retrieved exemplar database. No weight update; the agent's policy is shaped purely through which trajectories populate and are retrieved from the database (a reusable experience/skill store).
requires_training: none (no gradient updates to the agent; 'training' = growing and curating an in-context example database). The paper also shows in an appendix that the self-generated trajectories can additionally be used for SFT, but the core method requires no fine-tuning.
reward_or_critic_model: verifiable reward (binary environment success signal selects which trajectories are stored); exemplar utility scores Q(tau) are computed from downstream retrieval-conditioned success rates (a value-estimation-style self-as-judge over trajectory usefulness). No trained reward model or separate critic network.
distillation_target: episodic-memory / reusable-skill: self-generated successful trajectories distilled into a curated retrievable database of in-context examples. (Appendix also demonstrates the same self-generated data can be distilled into model-weights via SFT, but that is secondary.)
emergent_vs_engineered: engineered (scaffold/algorithmic): a ReAct-style agent with an external trajectory database and explicit accumulation + population-based curation + utility-based exemplar selection. The improvement is from the data-curation loop, not RL-emergent reflective behavior in the model.
memory_type: long-term-episodic / skill-library: a database of self-generated successful trajectories used as in-context examples (with multi-key retrieval over reasoning).
memory_persistence: cross-task (and cross-episode): the trajectory database accumulates across many tasks during deployment, enabling continual learning and expanding coverage to new tasks without retraining.
memory_curation_mechanism: population-or-Pareto-selected + retrieval-gated utility pruning: (1) Trajectory Bootstrapping appends successful trajectories (append-only base); (2) Database-level curation (DB-Cur) runs M parallel databases and copies the best-performing DB into the worst (population-based training, K doubling: 10,20,40,...); (3) Exemplar-level curation (EX-Cur) scores each trajectory by retrieval-conditioned success Q(tau) and retains only the top-1 trajectory per unique task goal, yielding a compact distilled DB.
error_localization_granularity: holistic/outcome-level: trajectories are kept or discarded based on whole-episode success; the method deliberately avoids step-level error attribution (failed trajectories are dropped to sidestep which-step-caused-failure ambiguity). Retrieval, however, operates at step level (re-retrieval at each step).
intra_task_vs_inter_task: inter-task: experience is transferred across tasks by reusing prior successful trajectories as in-context examples for new tasks (akin to Reflexion/ExpeL/AWM-style cross-task transfer), not within-a-single-task refinement.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: avoidance-only: improvement comes from steering future episodes toward patterns resembling past successes; there is no mid-trajectory self-correction or post-hoc revision of a failed run (failed trajectories are discarded).
task_domains: decision-making / embodied-text (household navigation & object manipulation), code (interactive SQL/tool-use), and a crafting/reasoning game
headline_result: On ALFWorld, success rises from 73% (Fixed-DB baseline) to 93% with the full method (Traj-BS + DB-Cur + EX-Cur), a +20pp gain using GPT-4o-mini; surpasses approaches using more powerful LLMs and hand-crafted components. Naive trajectory accumulation alone lifts ALFWorld 73%->89%, Wordcraft 55%->64%, InterCode-SQL 75%->79%.
baselines: Fixed-DB (fixed in-context example database / ReAct with static exemplars); upgrading model GPT-4o-mini -> GPT-4o; multiple test-time attempts (1->5 retries); task-specific human engineering (AutoManual, Chen et al. 2024); hierarchical approaches (Fu et al. 2024); ReAct-Finetune (SFT comparison in appendix).
gains_vs_baseline: ALFWorld +20pp over Fixed-DB (73%->93%); Traj-BS alone adds +16/+4/+9 pp on ALFWorld/InterCode-SQL/Wordcraft. The +20pp self-curation gain on ALFWorld exceeds the +15pp from upgrading GPT-4o-mini to GPT-4o and the +18pp from AutoManual's human engineering, and nearly matches the +23pp from 5 test-time retries while using only a single inference pass. DB-Cur raises ALFWorld 0.89->0.91; EX-Cur gives the largest Wordcraft boost (+8pp to 0.72) and +2pp InterCode-SQL; combined curation reaches 0.93 ALFWorld and 0.82 InterCode-SQL.
compute_cost_profile: Test-time: ~1x single inference pass (no extra test-time retries or success verification needed), the key efficiency claim vs test-time scaling. Training/build-time overhead: maintaining M parallel databases (up to 2x when combining both curation methods) and retrieval at every step over hundreds/thousands of accumulated trajectories; reviewers noted total build + per-step retrieval costs are not exhaustively analyzed. During DB construction, build-time success rates were ~81.3% (ALFWorld), 76.9% (InterCode), 58.6% (Wordcraft), so 18.7/23.1/41.4% of attempts are discarded.
known_limitations: (1) Failed trajectories are discarded -> potential inefficiency of wasted LLM calls (left as future work). (2) Gains may partly reflect accumulating a critical mass of exemplars covering the relatively small test distribution (e.g., ALFWorld test = 134 tasks across 6 types; retrieved exemplars may be very similar to test tasks). (3) Results limited to GPT-4o-mini, limiting generalizability across model families. (4) Build-time/retrieval compute not fully analyzed; DB-Cur adds variance-reduction but extra compute. (5) Avoidance-only — no mechanism to correct in-flight failures.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: env-reward: the method depends on the environment providing a binary success/failure signal to decide which trajectories to store; no per-step ground-truth labels and no self-verification of intermediate steps. Improvement is driven by environment-verified successes, not intrinsic self-critique.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive (task-dependent magnitude): consistent gains across all three benchmarks (largest on ALFWorld +20pp, smaller on InterCode-SQL). Because retention is gated by environment success rather than self-judgment, it avoids the label-leakage / intrinsic-self-correction failure mode; gains scale with accumulated experience.
calibration_effect: not-measured (no analysis of model confidence/calibration; the method targets task success rate, not calibration of a reasoning model).
failure_attribution_capability: n/a — the method explicitly avoids failure attribution; failed trajectories are discarded precisely to sidestep step-level which-step-caused-failure attribution ambiguity.
failure_mode_addressed: Targets weak/under-specified task policies by injecting environment-verified successful exemplars; mitigates run-to-run variability via population-based DB curation and low-utility/redundant exemplar accumulation via utility-based pruning. Does not address self-reflection-specific failure modes (superficial self-reflection, error-loops) since it does not perform verbal reflection.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new benchmark released; code and starter databases (ALFWorld, Wordcraft) released at github.com/VSAnimator/llm_self_improvement. Self-generated trajectory databases are produced by the method rather than published as a fixed dataset.
builds_on: ReAct (Yao et al.); Reflexion / ExpeL (verbal experience reuse, in-context cross-task transfer); reward-weighted regression (RL); population-based training (Jaderberg et al.); in-context RL / algorithm distillation (Laskin et al. 2023, Lee et al. 2023); retrieval-augmented in-context learning. Benchmarks: ALFWorld (Shridhar et al. 2020), InterCode-SQL (Yang et al. 2023), Wordcraft.
citation_count: ~25 (Google Scholar / arXiv 'Cited by 25' as of mid-2026)
reasoning_model_native: no — evaluated only with GPT-4o-mini (a non-reasoning model); the mechanism is model-agnostic scaffolding and is not specific to o1/R1-style reasoning models with built-in reflection.
on_policy_distillation_link: Strong conceptual link: trajectory bootstrapping is described as analogous to reward-weighted regression and learns only from the agent's own (on-policy) successful rollouts. The self-generated, environment-verified trajectories form an on-policy experience corpus that improves the policy in-context, and the paper shows the same data can be distilled into weights via SFT (an on-policy-distillation-style use of self-generated data).
sample_efficiency: Gains accrue as the database grows over hundreds-to-thousands of task attempts; performance scales with accumulated experience. DB-Cur uses K-doubling evaluation windows (10,20,40,...). Exact #trials to reach 93% on ALFWorld not pinned to a single number, but build-time used 5 training runs; the method matches a 5-attempt test-time-retry baseline using only 1 test-time pass.
